newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: NESTLE HAPPY WITH OREAL SITUATION.
newsitem.headline: NESTLE HAPPY WITH OREAL SITUATION.

text.p: Nestle SA is content with its current stake in L'Oreal, but envisages taking a majority stake and uniting it in a holding company grouping the world's biggest food and cosmetics groups, Nestle chairman Helmut Maucher said on Tuesday.

"No change is being planned" in Nestle's 49 percent stake in Gesparal, the company that controls French-based L'Oreal, Maucher told the company's annual news conference, dismissing a suggestion that Nestle might sell its stake to L'Oreal.
The Bettencourt family owns the other 51 percent stake. Maucher said he did not expect the family to sell it in the near future, but added that the partners were open to discussions.
"The future is open," he said, adding Nestle enjoyed good ties with the family and L'Oreal chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones.
Maucher envisaged one day uniting the groups in a holding company, but made clear L'Oreal would remain an independent company even if Nestle were eventually able to acquire a majority in it.
He said Nestle could one day be forced to make a takeover bid for L'Oreal if French legislation changed, but this was not Nestle's intention.
"We are very happy with the current situation," he said.
